title: What If the World Ran Out of Lithium? The Numbers Say Not Soon

scenes.text: What if the world ran out of lithium? Phones, laptops and electric cars all depend on it.
About 88 percent of the world's lithium goes into batteries.
The USGS counts about 37 million tonnes in reserves, and mines produced roughly 290,000 tonnes in 2025.
At that pace, known reserves last over a century, and the USGS lists about 150 million tonnes of resources.
The USGS expects world production capacity to double by 2029, and the US is still hunting new deposits.
So the squeeze won't be the ground running dry. It will be who refines it and how fast.
